0.0.n: A polite way to address a group, with さん adding respect.

0.2.n: A neutral, polite way to refer to yourself.

0.3.n: Marks 私 as the topic: the person this sentence is about.

0.4.n: Combines with 月 to make 10月, meaning October.

0.5.n: After a number, 月 names a calendar month; 10月 is October.

0.6.n: Marks October as the time when the trip happened.

0.7.n: This is the Japanese name of the country Slovenia.

0.8.n: Marks Slovenia as the destination of 行きました.

0.9.n: With に行く, this noun expresses the purpose of going.

0.10.n: Marks 旅行 as the purpose of going, rather than the destination.

0.11.n: The polite past form of 行く, showing that the trip already happened.

1.0.n: This is a country name, followed by に to show where the friend lives.

1.1.n: With 住む, に marks the place where someone lives.

1.2.n: Combines with の to describe the friend as mine.

1.3.n: Links 私 to 友達; 私の友達 means my friend.

1.4.n: Japanese nouns usually do not mark singular or plural; the translation here treats this as one friend.

1.5.n: Identifies 私の友達 as the person who lives in Slovenia.

1.6.n: The て-form of 住む plus います politely describes an ongoing state of residence.

2.0.n: The earlier sentence supplies whose friend this is, so 私の is left out.

2.1.n: Marks the person the speaker wanted to meet; 会う commonly uses に for that person.

2.2.n: 会う becomes 会いたい for wanting to meet; たかった makes it past, and です adds politeness.

3.0.n: Connects the previous wish to see the friend with the resulting trip.

3.2.n: Explicitly identifies the speaker, though Japanese often leaves this out when clear.

3.3.n: Marks 私 as the topic of the statement.

3.4.n: This is the Japanese name of the country the speaker visited.

3.5.n: Marks Slovenia as the destination of the movement.

3.6.n: 行く changes to 行きました to describe a completed past action politely.

0.lit: Everyone, as for me, in October, to Slovenia, for a trip, went.
0.tip: The three に particles mark time, destination, and purpose, respectively.

1.tip: 住んでいます describes an ongoing living situation, not a temporary action happening right now.

2.lit: With my friend, wanted to meet.
2.tip: The ending たかった expresses a past wish; the speaker is understood without saying 私.

3.lit: So, as for me, to Slovenia went.
3.tip: だから links the reason in the previous sentence to its result here.
